chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I have memorized the Quran by heart — is reciting it from memory superior, or looking into the Mushaf?'
He said, so he said to me: 'Rather, recite it while looking into the Mushaf, for it is superior. Do you not know that looking into the Mushaf is an act of worship?'

key_terms.المصحف: The Mushaf — the physical written codex of the Quran; distinguished from the Quran as recitation
key_terms.ظهر القلب: By heart/from memory; literally 'the back of the heart', an Arabic idiom for memorization
key_terms.عبادة: An act of worship ('ibada); the term covers all acts of obedience and devotion to God

ai.seo_question: Is it better to recite the Quran from memory or while looking at the Mushaf?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked by Is'haq ibn Ammar whether it is better to recite the Quran from memory or while looking at the physical Mushaf. The Imam (AS) answered definitively that reciting while looking at the Mushaf is superior, adding the remarkable teaching that the very act of gazing at the Mushaf is itself an act of worship. This hadith is used by Shia jurisprudents to establish the spiritual merits of engaging with the written Quran.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! I have memorised the Quran by heart, reading it from memory so is it superior or looking into the Parchment (while reciting)?’
So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘But, recite and while looking into the Parchment, for it is superior. Do you not know that the looking into the Parchment is an act of worship?’
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Yahya ibn al- Mubarak from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Mu’awiyah ibn Wahab from Ishaq ibn ‘ Ammar who has said the following:

“Once I said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, I memorize the Holy Quran by heart and read from my memory, is that more virtuous or looking on a copy of the Holy Quran?’
The narrator has said that the Imam said to me, ‘It is better to look in a copy. Have you not heard that looking at a copy of the Holy Quran is an act of worship?”’
